comment: Manual additions on top of Spring AOT-generated hints. Spring's ErrorHandlingDeserializer Java-serializes the caught deserialization exception (via ObjectOutputStream) to pass it downstream as a Kafka record header. This is a runtime-only code path (only triggered by an actual malformed message), so Spring AOT's static analysis never traces it, and native-image fails with UnsupportedFeatureError (SerializationConstructorAccessor not found) the first time a poison-pill message is consumed in production. GraalVM requires EVERY class in the exception's superclass chain to be registered individually (not just the leaf and Throwable) -- walk the full chain with `javap` before adding entries here, or this keeps failing one superclass at a time. Confirmed chain for DeserializationException: DeserializationException -> KafkaException -> NestedRuntimeException -> RuntimeException -> Exception -> Throwable.
